questions.q: What question is a cash position primarily built to answer?
options: What will cash flow look like six months from now?
As of right now, how much usable cash sits in each account and how is it about to change?
Which transaction codes are unmapped?
What journal entries will Create Accounting generate next quarter?
questions.explain: A cash position is a short-horizon, account-by-account view of balance and near-term in/outflows — a right-now picture, not a long-range one.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the inputs that build a cash position?
options: The bank's own reported balance from the most recent statement
Reconciled transactions already confirmed against the bank
Transactions still open but expected imminently
A multi-year historical trend analysis
questions.explain: A cash position is built from real statement balances, reconciled transactions, and imminent known activity — not long-range historical trend analysis, which belongs to forecasting.

questions.q: Why is a cash position only as reliable as the reconciliation work behind it?
options: Because reconciliation and positioning are entirely unrelated processes
Because the position leans on real, reconciled statement balances — stale unreconciled items distort the picture
Because a cash position ignores bank statements entirely
Because positions are only built once a year
questions.explain: Since the position is built on real reconciled activity, an account with a backlog of stale unreconciled items will show a distorted, unreliable position.

questions.q: How does Cash Positioning differ from Cash Forecasting at a high level?
options: Positioning is short-horizon and transaction-grounded; forecasting looks further out and leans more on projection
They are exactly the same process with different names
Forecasting only applies to Payables, never Receivables
Positioning always covers a full fiscal year
questions.explain: Positioning answers 'what do I actually have' in the near term; forecasting answers 'what should I expect' over a longer horizon.

questions.q: In the worked example, why did Harborview Metals Inc.'s Treasury team decide not to transfer funds this week?
options: Because the projected balance was below the minimum target
Because the projected end-of-week balance was comfortably above their minimum balance target
Because the account had no reconciled transactions
Because a currency conversion was required
questions.explain: The projected $150,000 balance was comfortably above the $100,000 minimum balance target, so no transfer was needed.
